title: Supported Kummer projective-line arrows
statement:
Let $\ell,E,n,A,C,\tau$ be the finite site coordinates. For a Noetherian scheme $S$ where $\ell$ is invertible, let $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, $i:S\hookrightarrow P$ its infinity divisor, and choose $r\geq0$ with $\ell^{r+1}A=0$. Define $h^p$ as the $Lq^*\dashv Rq_*$ adjunct of $A_P\to i_*A_S\to A_P(1)[2]$, where the second map is the supported Cartier Kummer map and its target is identified by $\tau$. Define $u^p$ by the shifted twisted adjunction unit and canonical line pullback. Define $b^p=[u^p,h^p]$. This map is invertible. Define $t_q^p$ as the existing projective-line projection-trace construction applied to the isomorphism with hom $b^p$, equivalently $(b^p)^{-1}$ followed by the second projection.

proof.text: For a square of left adjoints, the composite of the comparison of an adjunct with the right-adjoint counit mate is the adjunct of the compared original arrow. Naturality of the left comparison and the adjunction triangle prove this identity. Apply it first to the shifted line pullback and then to the normalized Chern arrow. It identifies the two components of projectiveB with the components of geoP1TwistedMap.

proof.text: Biproduct hom extensionality identifies projectiveB with geoP1TwistedMap. The existing projective-line decomposition theorem proves that map invertible: exact comparison preserves its biproduct and isomorphism, and the canonical direct-image mate is invertible on the shifted degree-zero line. Thus projectiveB_isIso. The existing definition projectiveTrace is consequently the inverse followed by the second projection.
